# Disagreement Log — Apocalypse of Peter, Chapter 14
**Agents:** EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 11

---

## Verse-by-Verse Disagreements

### v.1 — "kept the virginity of their body" vs. "preserved the virginity" vs. "kept their bodies in purity and virginity"
- **EMET:** "kept the virginity of their body"
- **LOGOS:** "preserved the virginity of their body"
- **PNEUMA:** "kept their bodies in purity and virginity"
- **Note:** PNEUMA adds "purity" as a second term; "purity and virginity" is not in source, which uses one term.

### v.2 — "suffered for the sake of righteousness" vs. "suffered for righteousness' sake"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "suffered for righteousness' sake"
- **PNEUMA:** "suffered for the sake of righteousness"
- **Note:** Equivalent. Minor word-order disagreement.

### v.4 — "This is a more glorious place" vs. "God has prepared a more glorious place"
- **EMET:** "This is a more glorious place which God prepared"
- **LOGOS:** "This is a more glorious place, prepared by God"
- **PNEUMA:** "God prepared a more glorious place still"
- **Note:** PNEUMA's "still" adds a superlative emphasis. Minor.

### v.5 — "very great gladness"
- All agents agree. No disagreement.

### v.6 — "angels of light and the seraphim above them"
- All agents agree on this. PNEUMA adds "and above them the seraphim" for clarity — the layered hierarchy is preserved by all.

### v.6 — "brilliant white light" vs. "great white light"
- **EMET:** "a great white light"
- **LOGOS:** "brilliant white light"
- **PNEUMA:** "a great white light"
- **Note:** "Brilliant" (LOGOS) is an intensification of "great." Minor.

### v.7 — "I was overwhelmed with wonder and joy" (PNEUMA)
- **EMET:** "I marveled greatly and rejoiced"
- **LOGOS:** "I marveled greatly and rejoiced"
- **PNEUMA:** "I was overwhelmed with wonder and joy"
- **Note:** "Overwhelmed" is PNEUMA's intensification. "Marveled greatly and rejoiced" is the literal rendering.

### v.9 — Peter's intercession framing
- **EMET:** Direct question format.
- **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** Slightly more conversational.
- **Note:** All three preserve the scriptural appeal; minor framing differences only.

### v.10 — "Hear me, Peter" vs. "Listen, Peter"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "Hear me, Peter"
- **PNEUMA:** "Listen, Peter"
- **Note:** Equivalent. "Hear me" (EMET/LOGOS) preserves the imperative register of the original more closely.

### v.11 — "and some will not be saved; they will go to the place of punishment forever"
- All agents agree on this verse. No significant disagreement.

### v.12 — "Those I have received from below" — "delivered" wording
- **EMET:** "Those whom I have received from below shall receive mercy through me, whom I have delivered"
- **LOGOS:** "Those whom I have received from below — I have delivered them — these shall receive mercy"
- **PNEUMA:** "Those I have received from below — those I have delivered — they will find mercy"
- **Note:** All three preserve the substance. The pronoun structure of EMET's "whom I have delivered" is ambiguous (does "whom" refer to Peter or to those delivered?). LOGOS's clarification is better.

---
*11 disagreements. SOPHIA: "preserved the virginity" (v.1); "marveled greatly and rejoiced" (v.7); "Hear me" (v.10); LOGOS structure for v.12.*
